differences.title: 1. INITIAL LOAD
differences.leftDesc: HTML sent from server, less JS needed for first paint.
differences.rightDesc: HTML often empty, requires JS to hydrate and render.

differences.title: 2. SEO
differences.leftDesc: Search engines easily crawl fully rendered HTML content.
differences.rightDesc: Requires JS execution for content, can impact indexing.

differences.title: 3. PERFORMANCE
differences.leftDesc: Faster Time To First Byte (TTFB) and Contentful Paint.
differences.rightDesc: Initial load time depends on client-side JavaScript processing.

differences.title: 4. INTERACTIVITY
differences.leftDesc: Client needs to re-render and attach event listeners.
differences.rightDesc: Interactive upon download and execution of JS bundle.

differences.title: 5. BANDWIDTH
differences.leftDesc: Sends pre-rendered HTML, reduces initial JavaScript payload.
differences.rightDesc: Requires larger JavaScript bundles to be downloaded and parsed.

differences.title: 6. COMPLEXITY
differences.leftDesc: Server handles rendering logic, potentially more resource intensive.
differences.rightDesc: Client handles rendering and state management, complex JS.

differences.title: 7. STATE MANAGEMENT
differences.leftDesc: State often managed on the server or passed via props.
differences.rightDesc: State managed entirely within the browser's JavaScript environment.
